problem_framing.rationale: The key-questions slide restates the decision exactly as posed (enter or not, and by which route) and lists all five board objectives and constraints as success criteria, including the one-launch bandwidth limit. These are then used as the tests for each option (cap, payback, margin floor, revenue vs ambition) in the body and in the three-way comparison with Japan. The issues the answer turns on (ACoS vs the benchmark, awareness vs the sell-through cut-off, the ambition gap) are identified in the executive summary. It also flags its reading of 'on the way to $40M' as a direction for the board to confirm. 'No US entry' is only handled through the Japan option, which is reasonable given the bandwidth constraint.

storyline_coherence.rationale: The governing thought answers the question, the five summary points are the five sections, and almost every title is a claim that its slide supports; the titles alone give the argument. Flaws: (1) slide 6 says 'most new spend is going to Korean brands' beside its own 38.6% share-of-growth figure; (2) the summary says Japan becomes the better choice above 28.6% ACoS, while slide 31 shows Japan returns more cash by 2030 at anything above roughly plan ACoS, so the US case really rests on scale rather than the payback threshold, and this is not carried cleanly into the summary; (3) section-summary slides (5, 12, 18, 26) restate what the following slides show, and the repeated divider slides all carry the same title. Strong hierarchy with some redundancy and one small internal inconsistency.

evidence_and_reasoning.rationale: I re-derived the main models and they match the pack and the key: Amazon contribution $4.725 at 25% ACoS and $3.05 at 32%, retail $7.55, Option A cumulative cash $2.40M / $0.38M / -$2.32M at 25/28/32% ACoS, break-even ACoS 28.56%, tariff cases (-$0.74M at 28% ACoS with 25% duty), Option B cumulative cash -$9.48M to -$20.80M, group margin 4.46% (B) and 9.45% (A) in 2027, Japan $1.8M, stall case -$6.98M, halo contribution $3.98M against $31.6M retail cost. All four critical evidence items are used, including evidence that cuts against the recommendation (32% benchmark, stalled Amazon-first peers, repeat below Korea). The correlation critique is sound. Flaws: 'most new spend is going to Korean brands' contradicts the deck's own 38.6%; several pilot claims go beyond the pack ('sign of word of mouth', 'no discounting needed', 'rate it as Korean buyers do', 'pilot understates what a full range can do'); the slowing month-on-month pilot growth (about 17% to about 9%) is not noted; the $44.2M-in-2032 extrapolation holds a 29% growth rate constant although forecast growth is decelerating (87%, 52%, 29%), and it underpins 'the gap is one of timing'; 'tariff alone would not break the case' is true only from the 25% plan ACoS the deck itself doubts (its own table shows it fails at pilot ACoS). Option B is not re-run at 2.6 units per door. Excellent quantitative work with a handful of overstated claims.

strategic_judgment.rationale: A clear recommendation that follows from the analysis: Amazon-led entry with five quantified gates (ACoS 28.6%, repeat 31%, revenue, peak cash $3.9M, awareness 20% before retail), each with a response, plus owners and dated next steps. Options A, B and J are compared on the board's own criteria; retail is rejected on cap, margin floor, sell-through and a non-causal halo; Japan is treated as a real alternative and named as the fallback. The deck states what must hold (ACoS at or below 28.6%), is candid that the benchmark case misses payback and that Japan returns more cash unless ACoS holds at plan, bounds the downside (about $7M in the stall case, $3.9M under cost stress), and says the ambition is not reached by 2030. It revises the CEO's retail trigger on evidence (15% to 20%, since the 10-20% band median of 3.5 is below the 4.0 cut-off). It avoids all the key's traps. Minor weaknesses: the 'two years late' framing of the ambition is rosy, the mechanics and cost of a switch to Japan are not worked through, the repeat gate (31%) is already above the pilot's 29%, and a lower-fixed-cost variant is not considered. None is material enough to change the decision.

clarity_and_concision.rationale: The answer is on slide 3 and the language is plain and precise, with quantified titles. But the deck runs to 45 slides and about 7,000 words for a three-option decision: five repeated agenda slides, four section-summary slides that duplicate their sections, a risk table that overlaps the gates table, and several market slides (6-8) that could be one. Backups are appropriately separated. Length is clearly out of proportion to the decision even though individual slides are crisp.

unsupported_claims.quote: Every month up: growth never paused, a sign of word of mouth and reviews, not a one-off promotion
unsupported_claims.why: The pack gives monthly units only; nothing on what drove growth (ads, promotions, word of mouth). Causal attribution is invented, and the slowing monthly growth rate is not mentioned.

unsupported_claims.quote: At $24.00 a unit: the pilot sold at the price the plan uses, with no discounting needed
unsupported_claims.why: The pack gives an average selling price of $24.00; it says nothing about whether discounts or promotions were used.

unsupported_claims.quote: Product quality travels: US buyers rate it as Korean buyers do
unsupported_claims.why: The pack contains no Korean rating data to compare with the 4.5-star US rating.

unsupported_claims.quote: Other brands: grew slowly, so most new spend is going to Korean brands
unsupported_claims.why: Table 1 shows K-beauty took $1.7B of $4.4B category growth (38.6%, as the slide itself states); most new spend went to other brands.

unsupported_claims.quote: 2030: growth is still close to a third a year, so the gap is one of timing
unsupported_claims.why: Rests on holding 29% growth for two years beyond the forecast horizon, although forecast growth is decelerating (87%, 52%, 29%); the pack gives no basis for 2031-32.

unsupported_claims.quote: Three SKUs only: the 2027 plan adds four more, so the pilot understates what a full range can do
unsupported_claims.why: The planning forecast already includes the four extra SKUs, and the pack says it is unclear whether more SKUs lift repeat; the pack does not show the pilot understating potential.
The pack reports Yeoreum's revenue (below $5M) but gives no loss or cost data for the stalled Amazon-first brands.

unsupported_claims.quote: Social media builds awareness and Amazon closes the sale: Onsoo needs no shelf space to build its brand
unsupported_claims.why: Survey shares of discovery and purchase channel do not establish that Onsoo can build awareness without retail; its aided awareness is still 4% after the pilot.

unsupported_claims.quote: Saebom added 300 doors in 2025, three years after an Amazon-first entry, once it had about $30M of US revenue
unsupported_claims.why: The pack gives about $30M as 2025 revenue and doors added in 2025; it does not say revenue reached $30M before the doors were added.

numerical_errors.quote: Other brands: grew slowly, so most new spend is going to Korean brands
numerical_errors.correct: K-beauty captured $1.7B of the $4.4B category growth in 2021-25 (38.6%); other brands captured $2.7B (61.4%), so most new spend did not go to Korean brands.

logical_contradictions.quote_a: K-beauty share of the category's growth 38.6%
logical_contradictions.quote_b: Other brands: grew slowly, so most new spend is going to Korean brands
logical_contradictions.why: A 38.6% share of category growth means the majority of new spend went to non-Korean brands; the two statements on the same slide cannot both be true.

recommendation.summary: Approve an Amazon-led US launch in 2027 with five quarterly gates led by ACoS at or below the 28.6% payback break-even; reject the national retail launch; add only a targeted retail test once aided awareness passes 20%; keep the Japan scale-up as the fallback if ACoS stays above break-even; treat $40M as a direction reached after 2030.
recommendation.rationale: Meets all four defensibility criteria: options are compared on cap, payback and margin floor; the 25% ACoS and 4.5 units-per-door assumptions are tested against the 32% and 2.6 benchmarks; the payback condition and the triggers for slowing or switching are stated; and the deck says Option A reaches only two-thirds of the $40M ambition by 2030 while B gets closer only by breaking the cap. The 2032 extrapolation that softens the ambition gap is optimistic but is labelled as conditional and flagged for the board.

hypothesis_handling.rationale: The deck keeps the CEO's Amazon-first route and changes three things on evidence: the retail trigger rises from 15% to 20% awareness (the 10-20% band median of 3.5 is below the 4.0 cut-off), ACoS is gated at the 28.6% break-even instead of assumed at 25%, and retail becomes a targeted test rather than a 2029 roll-out. It confronts the 25% plan ACoS with the 32% benchmark, the 4.5 units per door with the 2.6 median, and the 0.71 correlation with reverse and common causation. It says the benchmark case misses payback and that Japan returns more cash unless ACoS holds at plan. This matches the expected keep-with-conditions handling. The unsupported causal claims are on the pilot (growth as 'a sign of word of mouth') and on social media building the brand without shelf space.

output.overall_comment: Weighted score 4.3 (framing 5, coherence 4, evidence 4, judgment 5, clarity 3). A rigorous, well-argued document whose models reproduce the answer key almost exactly: unit economics, Option A cash under the ACoS and tariff sensitivities, the 28.6% break-even, Option B's $20.8M cash need and 4.5% group margin, and the Japan comparison. It tests both planning assumptions against the benchmarks, dismantles the halo correlation, avoids every trap, and lands on a gated Amazon-led entry with Japan as fallback, which is the key's preferred defensible answer. Weaknesses: one self-contradicting market claim ('most new spend is going to Korean brands' beside a 38.6% share of growth); several over-read pilot claims (word of mouth, no discounting, parity with Korean ratings); an optimistic constant-growth extrapolation to $44M in 2032 that softens the ambition gap; a 'tariff alone does not break the case' framing that holds only at the plan ACoS the deck itself doubts; and considerable length and repetition (45 slides, repeated dividers and section summaries) for a three-option decision.
